# Architecture Decision Records

> Decision records for Rocky Surf's open-source v0.1. Each link is a self-contained ADR.
> Newest decisions reflect current intent; superseded ones are kept for history.
> Statuses: Proposed | Accepted | Deprecated | Superseded by ADR-NNNN | Rejected.
>
> ADRs 0001-0004 are the Phase 3 design freeze (`rockysurf-q5lm.1`), written from
> `docs/spike/findings.md` — the de-risking spike's findings memo, which is the input
> contract for the freeze. Read that memo for the evidence behind any decision here.

## Control Plane & Runtime

- [0001 Replace the AWS-serverless control plane with one portable self-hosted app](0001-single-portable-control-plane-app.md): [Accepted] One Hono + Drizzle/SQLite + SSE + in-process-jobs app replaces ~48 Lambdas, 8 DynamoDB tables and 8 CFN stacks; per-server CloudFormation dropped; create ordering inverted; startup recovery is a requirement.

## Provisioning & Bootstrap

- [0002 Push bootstrap is the default; callback is a scoped fallback](0002-push-bootstrap-default-callback-fallback.md): [Accepted, amended by 0008] Inert ~2.1KB cloud-config plus outbound SSH is the default; callback verified on real cloud-init (q5lm.5) and kept, but scoped to already-reachable hosted cores because a NAT'd core needed a reverse tunnel to use it; embedded stays cut; two tokens with two lifetimes, short TTL over strict single-use.
- [0010 A failed tool install terminates the box; the report is the diagnosis](0010-failed-tool-install-terminates-the-box.md): [Accepted] Owner ruling 2026-08-26 (issue #119): a failed TOOL install releases the instance (`bootstrap.onFailure: terminate | keep`, default terminate) after core has captured the whole step log over SSH; every other failure keeps the machine. Repository clones become optional steps and surface as warnings on a running box. One `failBootstrap()` path serves push and callback mode (callback failures were previously unrecorded until the 30-minute timeout). A `failed` row no longer auto-flips to `terminated` when its machine vanishes — it stays visible with its explanation until the user dismisses it. Amends 0008's "stays diagnosable" for the tool case. Amended 2026-08-30 (#168): the report's agent-log tail (~200 lines — the whole install log) is now rendered on the server page as the whole-setup install log, and callback mode's terminal failure POST carries it as `agentLog`.
- [0012 The agent retries an apt fetch failure twice for every step, then fails the launch by URL](0012-apt-retry-is-the-agents-standard.md): [Accepted, amended by 0015] Issue #188. The apt retry becomes a tool-install standard the AGENT guarantees — two attempts per step, each step with its own budget, replacing the one-retry-per-bootstrap that a first flaky step used to spend on everyone's behalf; between attempts the regional-mirror swap (once per bootstrap, nothing left to swap after) or a bounded wait, then `apt-get update`. An `Acquire::Retries` drop-in was rejected on this repo's own measurements: it retries the transfer against the index apt already has, and neither a 503 nor a 404 is retried at any setting. A step that fails twice still terminates the box (ADR-0010) and the failure report now names the URL that would not serve, blames the mirror rather than the pack, and says to test it and create again. Pack authors are told not to write their own apt retry; `curl` stays theirs at `--retry 3`.
- [0015 A step that says nothing is announced on the journal while it lasts](0015-a-quiet-step-announces-itself.md): [Accepted] Issue #205. The owner terminated a healthy box at five minutes because "Installing tools" had not moved: its first apt step was waiting on a mirror slow to answer (the same step took 4 min 21 s on their previous launch that day), `apt-get update -qq` prints nothing until it succeeds or gives up, and the #129 notice covers only the wait BETWEEN two attempts. Now the agent watches each step's log and, after `ROCKYSURF_STEP_QUIET_S` (60) of silence, posts the existing `notice` — "build-essential has said nothing for 4 min … Nothing is stuck." — re-posted each minute with the elapsed time and withdrawn on the next byte or the step's end. Measured in polls (five a second) rather than `$SECONDS`; the step runs as a background pipeline with its exit status through a file. Amends 0012 clause 3 on the owner's ruling: the RETRY is announced too — the moment a first apt attempt fails, the notice names what could not be downloaded and from where (the `Failed to fetch` URL and status), the swap or wait and the one more attempt, the derived bound ("gives up after 32 more minutes at most": the step's own timeout plus the wait) and the choice — wait, or terminate now (the existing button) and launch on another provider; the `apt-mirror` failure report closes with the same two options in the same words. Worst case for a tool step is 62 minutes (two 30-minute attempts, the 2-minute wait) and then failure by URL; nothing waits indefinitely. Core and the SPA are unchanged except the callback `notice` cap (300 → 1000). A browser-side timer (cannot say why), an apt `Timeout` drop-in (unmeasured on a real box) and a shorter stall guard (the step was healthy) were rejected. The 409s in the screenshot were the Tools page correctly refusing to delete or re-create a tool a pack uses.
- [0011 A user-supplied script is one more plan step, run last and optional](0011-user-script-at-create-time.md): [Accepted] Issue #184: the person creating a server may hand the box a script, EC2-user-data style, and choose whether it runs as `root` or `rocky` — the freedom EC2 does not give. It is one more singleton step id (`user-script`) rather than a new mechanism, so `PLAN_VERSION` stays 1: version 1 froze the FIELDS, not the id namespace. Phase 5, after everything the pack contributes and before core's own finishing steps, because those all report `ready` and a later report is refused in callback mode. `optional: true` on 0010's own rule — every tool is installed and every repo cloned, so a failed script is a warning on a running box, never a confiscated machine. Plain text on the row and in the plan snapshot (encrypting one copy beside a cleartext one is custody theatre), bounded at EC2's 16 KiB, not echoed on any route, with `running_user_script` joining the progress vocabulary as "Running your script".
- [0008 A supplied key retires core's own managed key once bootstrap confirms it](0008-supplied-key-retires-managed-key.md): [Accepted, amended by 0010] Amends 0002 for the supplied-key case: a required, last plan step surgically removes core's own `authorized_keys` line — never a rewrite, which would delete a BYO operator's pre-existing access — once it confirms the user's own key is authorized; core then retires the stored private half but keeps the host half for `/ssh-host-key`. Same trigger point in both bootstrap topologies: the row reaching `running`.

## Provider SDK

- [0003 Freeze the provider SDK shape, with deliberate exclusions](0003-provider-sdk-shape-and-exclusions.md): [Accepted, amended by 0009, 0021, 0025, 0026 and 0027] Adopts A1-A7, B1-B3, C1-C3, D1-D6, E2/E4, F1-F2; adds `terminating`, `Offering.available`, resource ownership and a propagation grace on `describe()`; rejects `dedupeName`, `hostKeys` and a tenth error code; spot/resize stay cut. The "dynamic out-of-tree plugin loading" exclusion was lifted by 0026; post-freeze amendments E12–E19 each add optional fields a provider could not tell the truth without.
- [0025 Whether a stopped machine still bills is a capability, and the meter reads it](0025-billing-while-stopped-is-a-capability.md): [Accepted] Issue #294, gap S1 of the DigitalOcean audit. `ProviderCapabilities.billsWhileStopped?: boolean`, absent = false (ADR-0003 amendment E17): a `stopped` instance accrues at the SAME hourly rate; a reduced-rate cloud MUST NOT set it and files an ADR question instead, never an approximation. Core records the provider's answer on the server row (`servers.bills_while_stopped`, migration 0020) beside `providerState`, written by `recordProviderState` at both lifecycle reads and refreshed on every read, so `isBillingRow` stays a pure function of the row and a cloud switched OFF in the config cannot silently stop the meter on a machine it is still charging for — the live-registry-lookup shape was rejected in review for exactly that under-reporting. `billingStatesFor(row)` is the base list plus `stopped` when the row says so; the `billingSince` anchor uses the same rule. Every front end learns it through the `billing` block it already reads: the server page prints "Stopped, and still billing", New Server warns before the machine exists, MCP `list_providers` carries the optional capabilities and names the flag as the thing to check before `stop_server`, and the web bundle imports the SDK's capability type instead of a drifted hand copy. Conformance checks the optional capabilities are booleans when present. A billing-model enum, `stop: false` for DigitalOcean, and advisory text alone were each rejected.
- [0026 A personal provider is an npm package named in the config file, loaded with Rocky Surf's full access](0026-a-personal-provider-is-a-package-named-in-the-config-file.md): [Accepted, amended 2026-09-05] Issue #294, item 2 of the settled direction. `providers.<id>.package` — an npm name resolved from `<dataDir>/providers` (`~/.rockysurf/providers`; `/data/providers` in the container, so it survives `npx rockysurf@latest`, a rebuild and an image rebuild) or a path — is loaded ONCE before boot by the composition root (`import()` is async; composition is synchronous and re-run on config change, so `BootOptions.providers` may return a promise only at boot), every section loaded whether enabled or not so a personal cloud can be switched on from Settings without a restart, and a section added after boot reported "restart to load its package". Every failure (not found, throws on import, not a factory, id disagrees with the section key) is an unavailable-provider reason, never fatal. The `providers` schema stays strict for the shipped five and admits another key only with `package:` (catchall on the INNER object, typed `unknown` so no shipped section's type widens; "did you mean hetzner?" for a one-edit typo; lowercase hostname-safe ids); `preferences.tiers` admits any key and the top-level refine refuses one naming no provider — the standalone `preferencesSchema` `live-preferences.ts` parses alone must stay permissive. Resolution finds the manifest with `module.findPackageJSON` (guarded; fallback `node_modules/<name>/package.json`) and reads `exports` `import`→`node`→`default`→`require` LAST and never refused, then `module`, `main`, `index.js` — because `createRequire().resolve()` fails on every provider package this repo ships (import-only exports). `isProviderError` becomes STRUCTURAL (name + a frozen code) since a personal package carries its own SDK copy. E18: `ProviderFactory.credentialEnv`/`credentialField`, optional; the registry carries a `ProviderDescriptor` per known factory so the wizard names a disabled personal cloud and detects its variable. `settings/inventory.ts` builds the inventory per file: every personal section gets `enabled`, `package` (restart) and read-only `sizes` plus a section titled by the factory's displayName, and `redactTree` takes the inventory's predicate so every OTHER leaf of a personal section is masked by default (`SECRET_KEY_NAME` knows `token`, not `privateKey`). Trust model: full trust, no sandbox, one sentence verbatim in self-hosting.md, writing-a-provider.md, SECURITY.md, the panel and the boot log — "a provider runs with Rocky Surf's full access — install ones you trust." A `personalProviders:` block, a typed catchall, loading inside composition, resolving from the app's own `node_modules`, refusing require-only entries, an SDK-redirecting loader hook and a key-name credential heuristic were each rejected. **Amended 2026-09-05 (owner ruling, reverting PR #390):** personal providers are verified by their AUTHOR AND INSTALLER, not by this repository's nightly — a nightly real-cloud leg is for OFFICIAL providers, the ones composed into `packages/rockysurf/src/compose.ts`, and a personal provider ships a fully daggered capability column (the `byo` column is the model). `packages/provider-digitalocean` stays as the worked example, with its tarball install test; its nightly leg, `deploy/digitalocean/` and the DigitalOcean branches in `scripts/e2e/` were removed.
- [0009 AWS/Azure prices are served from a hosted feed, with no bundled fallback](0009-prices-served-from-hosted-feed.md): [Accepted] Amends 0003's live-pricing exclusion for the price table only: the `price-feed` workflow republishes normalized JSON to GitHub Pages daily and installations read it at runtime, so a price change never needs a release; feed unreachable means `hourly: null` everywhere and everything else keeps working — a bundled fallback was explicitly rejected by the owner. Catalogues (AWS type shapes, Azure size list) stay bundled; the reader rejects a whole document on any invalid price because the spend cap consumes these numbers; the nightly `price-drift` job and `--check` are retired. **Amended 2026-08-25 (rockysurf-ndx6):** GCP joined the feed for consistency — its hand-transcribed numbers now live in `scripts/gcp-transcribed-prices.json` and publish as `gcp.json`, with `fetchedAt` pinned to the TRANSCRIPTION date (per-row in `transcribedAt`) so a daily republish cannot launder stale hand-copied numbers as fresh. Hetzner stays off the feed.

- [0024 The offering/size resolver is one implementation, and it lives in the provider SDK](0024-one-offering-resolver-shared-through-the-sdk.md): [Accepted] Issue #349. The ~120 lines that decide which machine a t-shirt size buys existed twice — `packages/core/src/servers/offerings.ts` for the CLI and the MCP, `packages/web/src/lib/requirements.ts` for the browser, which is the copy that decides what gets BILLED on a browser create — with `scripts/check-size-table.mjs` comparing only the two `SIZE_REQUIREMENTS` tables and two parallel #124 test lists pinning neither copy against the other. The decisions move to `@rockysurf/provider-sdk`'s new `sizing.ts` (`SERVER_SIZES`, `SIZE_REQUIREMENTS`, `requirementsForSize`, `compareOfferingsByPrice`, `meetsRequirements`, `chooseOffering`, `preferenceObstacle`, `chooseForSize`) and both trees import it; resolution still runs CLIENT-SIDE before submit, because the page must quote the machine it posts (quote-what-you-showed) and a fully-specified create must never consult the catalogue (create-survives-a-pricing-outage). NOT a charter amendment: the SDK's promise, as its own `contract.test.ts` asserts, is zero runtime DEPENDENCIES, not zero code — `errors.ts`, `instance.ts`, `provision.ts` and `ssh-cidr.ts` (ADR-0021, for this same reason) already ship pure helpers; only the "Types only" description and README were stale, and the zero-import assertion is widened from the six frozen surface files to every source file because the SPA bundle now imports this package. PROSE IS NOT SHARED — the shared functions return structured outcomes (`OfferingRefusal` with `soldOut`/`requirements`/`unanimousReason`, a `PreferenceObstacle` of `not-offered`/`unavailable`/`arch-mismatch`) and each surface phrases them in its own unchanged voice, core's lowercase HTTP fragments and the SPA's sentences. `allowedOfferings`/`describeCatalogue` stay server-only, `availableArchitectures` and the price formatters stay in web, web's unused `alternatives` and its never-true `diskGb` clause are dropped, `SERVER_SIZES` is defined once and re-exported by core's `db/schema.ts`, and `check-size-table.mjs` is retired with its stale "only copy that decides" comment. A new workspace package (a twelfth published package and three hand-written counts for one file), a browser-safe subpath of core (better-sqlite3 and ssh2 in the tree — safety by care rather than by construction), moving resolution server-side (both pinned properties forbid it) and a shared phrasing dictionary (UI copy in a published SDK) were each rejected; the environment-parsing, `envRef` regex and `RDP_MIN_LENGTH` duplications the issue also lists were deliberately LEFT, none being about `Offering`.

- [0021 `sshAllowedCidr` is a list, and saving it pushes it at the clouds that enforce it](0021-ssh-access-is-pushed-on-save-not-only-on-provision.md): [Accepted] Issue #304. The setting becomes a LIST (a bare string still means a list of one, an empty list is refused, `0.0.0.0/0` anywhere still needs `allowAllCidr: true`, and overlapping ranges are deliberately never collapsed because a `/32` inside a `/24` means something to whoever wrote them), and a save now reaches the cloud: `POST /api/v1/network/ssh-access/sync` pushes the list at every provider declaring the new `managesSshAccess` capability, provisioning nothing, and skips any provider whose config file and running process disagree so it can never push a CIDR this process has not adopted. **Amends ADR-0003 E11**, which rejected `ensureAccess()` for having "no second implementation to generalize from" and said to revisit when a second provider needed the same call — three do, and it arrives as a capability flag plus `syncSshAccess()`, the first OPTIONAL method on the interface; that departs from A2's required-and-throwing precedent on the ground that a required method breaks providers written outside this repo while an undeclared capability costs them nothing, and core still branches on the FLAG rather than `typeof provider.x`. **Amends ADR-0017** in scope, not label: a `'save'` consumer may live outside this process, so `sshAllowedCidr` KEEPS `'save'` and the consumer was fixed — 0017's own risk note already called a stale `'save'` consumer "a bug in the consumer, not a reason to relabel" — with the push a separate, bounded, best-effort call that adoption never depends on. AWS deletes its process-lifetime `ingressEnsured` latch (a corrected CIDR used to need a restart), provisions additively, and REPORTS rather than revokes — it touches only ranges carrying its own `rockysurf sshAllowedCidr` stamp and hands back the exact `aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress` command for anything else, so it needs no new IAM permission. Azure stays a child-resource PUT of `securityRules/rockysurf-ssh` (`sourceAddressPrefixes` when plural) and needs no new permission either. GCP was the worst — `sourceRanges` written at create time and never again — and now patches (sending only `sourceRanges`), gated on the rule's description, WIDENING ONLY, never deleting and never delete-and-recreating (the rule is `ownership: 'shared'`, D1); a rule whose description does not match is left as found and reported `failed` rather than `skipped`; `compute.firewalls.update` is the one permission added, 22 → 23. Azure is the only cloud where REMOVING a CIDR takes effect in one step, because its rule is rewritten whole. Doing the push inside the settings save, runtime IP discovery (the standing ruling: a third party's availability must never decide a firewall rule), delete-and-recreate, and revoking anything Rocky Surf cannot prove it created were each rejected. Converging AWS and GCP to EXACTLY the list — revoking stamped extras, patching to the list alone — was deliberately NOT in the #304 release but **is now done in issue #309**: a stamped extra is offered keep-or-remove on the Settings page (default keep), REMOVE sends it back as a confirmed itemized revoke (AWS `ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress` as `RevokeSshOnOwnGroupOnly`, added authorize-before-revoke; GCP patches `sourceRanges` down, no new permission), provision stays additive and never revokes, and an unstamped range the operator asks to remove is surfaced as a failure with the manual command. **Amended 2026-09-04 (issue #294, gap S2):** a cloud whose firewall rules carry NO authorship field (DigitalOcean) treats the whole object Rocky Surf created and named as the unit of authorship — converge in one write, `removable` and `reported` always empty, Azure's shape; anti-lockout unchanged.

- [0027 A provider declares its settings and its advisories, and the Settings page is built from them](0027-a-provider-declares-its-settings-and-the-page-is-built-from-them.md): [Accepted] Issue #294, item 3 of the settled direction. `ProviderFactory.settings?` (ADR-0003 amendment E19) — a declaration DISTINCT from the zod config schema (which cannot be introspected without a dependency, carries no labels, does not know `enabled`/`package`/`sizes` are core's, cannot say a `token` box takes a variable NAME, and cannot say `sshAllowedCidr`+`allowAllCidr` is one control): title/help, fields with a closed set of kinds (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `secret`, `stringList`, `sshCidrList`) and their label/help/warning/writable/appliesAt/accepts/example, lists (the byo-hosts shape), an `offering` noun/example for the saved-type fields, and `advisories` for the `settings` or `create` surface. `assertSettingsShape` (run by `assertFactoryShape`) requires sentences, refuses the three reserved names, parses every `example` through `configSchema`, and requires `managesSshAccess` behind any `sshCidrList` by constructing the provider — a firewall control whose saves never reach the cloud is ADR-0021's defect. Core's `settings/inventory.ts` MERGES: a declaration (recorded on the registry as `ProviderDescriptor.settings`, loaded or not) becomes rows the page already draws — `enabled` first, declared fields in order with `allowAllCidr` implied after an `sshCidrList`, `sizes` last with the declared noun, `package` for personal, lists as cards, the three saved-type fields through the static table's own template; tab order is PRESERVED (`PROVIDER_ORDER` hetzner, aws, azure, gcp, byo; personal after, in file order — schema order would have moved Hetzner from first to fourth); redaction follows the declaration. The page renders declared rows with their own label/placeholder, draws `sshCidrList` with the CIDR control, derives the whitelist ledger from inventory paths (the `['aws','azure','gcp']` loop is gone), prints settings-advisories at a panel's head and create-advisories on New Server. HETZNER MIGRATED FIRST (rows, section, tier row and hand-written block deleted; prose moved verbatim onto the factory) so the declared path is exercised by the product, not a fixture. AMENDED 2026-09-05 (issue #370): AWS, Azure, GCP and BYO migrated too, so ALL SHIPPED PROVIDERS DECLARE — `fields.ts` holds no `providers.*` or `preferences.tiers.*` row, `TIER_PREFERENCE_CLOUDS` and the `providers.*` entries of `SETTINGS_LISTS` are gone, the SPA has no hand-written provider block, and the inventory is a pure function of the loaded factories plus core's own sections. That amendment adds three optional declaration fields (`ProviderSettingListItemField.help`; `offering.label`, the in-sentence name; `offering.allowlist: false`, no `sizes` key — BYO needs all three), names the splice anchors now that no static provider section is left to find, labels the read-only allowlist `Offered ${noun}s`, adds AWS's `securityGroupName`, and records what deliberately stayed static: `PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENV` for the three chain clouds (which have no credential FIELD at all), Azure's `allowAzureCli`, and the wizard's per-cloud steps. `fields.test.ts` gains `DECLARED_BY_PROVIDER` (its own set, not `DELIBERATELY_ABSENT`) for the credential scan and the enumeration; the composition root's `settings-parity.test.ts` asserts the factory declares every field core's mirrored section accepts and its credential as secret. Rendering the zod schema, zero migrations, all five migrations, a separately declared `allowAllCidr`, and schema-derived tab order were each rejected.
- [0028 Providers are distributed through the shop, and installing one is not running one](0028-providers-are-distributed-through-the-shop.md): [Accepted] Issue #374, item 5 of #294's settled direction. A registry publishes providers in a SEPARATE `providers.json` beside `index.json`, fetched from the same `registry.sources` — separate because `registryIndexSchema` is strict, so a `providers` array inside `index.json` would turn every installed client's pack shelf into "this is not a pack registry index"; a `.yaml` one-file source publishes no providers and says so rather than having a sibling URL guessed for it. An entry names `providerId` (the `providers:` section key, hostname-safe lowercase), name/description/version, the npm `package`, an **https-only** `tarball` and its `sha256`, a summary of the `settings` it will ask for, and its `capabilities` answers — all shown BEFORE consent, because they decide whether the provider is usable here at all. NO TRUST FIELD, and the strict schema refuses one: the sentence every listing carries verbatim — "a provider runs with Rocky Surf's full access — install ones you trust" — is `PERSONAL_PROVIDER_TRUST_SENTENCE`, a Rocky Surf constant put on the response by core, because a shop that could write it could soften it (ADR-0006 decision 2, applied to a heavier payload). Install is fetch (SSRF guard, 16 MiB wire cap) → digest → unpack with a reader written for this (`providers/tarball.ts`: no absolute paths, no `..`, no symlinks, no hard links, no device nodes, everything under `package/`, ≤4 000 files, ≤64 MiB uncompressed — the gzip-bomb cap the wire cap cannot see) → manifest `name` must match the listing → entry resolved by THE SAME resolver the loader uses (`resolvePackageEntry` moved into core for this) → every declared runtime dependency must already resolve → staged and renamed into place → `providers.<id>.package` + `enabled: true` written through the settings write path (Document API, `checkConfigText`, atomic write carrying the mode, then adopt — ADR-0017) → "restart required", always, because the package is imported once before boot. **Nothing is executed, ever**: no npm, no lifecycle scripts, `scripts` in a fetched manifest is data — so a shop provider must be SELF-CONTAINED (zero runtime deps or bundled), and the refusal names the missing packages. Update = re-install, REPLACING the tree; the installed version is read from the manifest on disk, never remembered, because an operator may `npm install` there by hand. Remove deletes the package and the whole section after a confirmation naming both, and is REFUSED while any non-terminated row names that provider. **AMENDED 2026-09-05 (owner ruling, issue #394): Rocky Surf neither lists nor installs providers.** The Providers tab is gone, the page is called Surge Packs again (three tabs, route `/packs` unchanged), and the whole in-app installer is deleted as dead code once nothing calls it — `providers/{install,tarball,tar.fixture,shop,shop-index,shop-routes}.ts` with their tests, the routes unmounted, `countServersOnProvider` gone with its only caller, and `packs/safe-fetch.ts` back to text-only with no `maxBytes`, so nothing raises the 2 MB import cap. `resolvePackageEntry`, `PERSONAL_PROVIDERS_DIRNAME`, `PERSONAL_PROVIDER_TRUST_SENTENCE` and `PersonalProviderManifest` STAY in core: the composition root's loader is a real caller. Decisions 3 and 5 are superseded; 1, 2 and 4 hold with the OPERATOR as the actor — `providers.json` is still the registry's document, still separate from `index.json`, still trust-field-free, now validated by the registry's CI alone. Installing is `tar -xzf` under `<dataDir>/providers` plus two config lines plus a restart, and the app's contribution is a one-line pointer at the shop's providers section on each provider tab of the SETTINGS page, because Settings is where a provider is configured. The trust sentence keeps its job and loses one venue (panels and boot log, not a listing). Keeping the installer for a hypothetical CLI subcommand, and keeping a read-only listing tab that links out, were both rejected. A `providers` array in `index.json`, a second source list, running `npm install`, installing without a dependency check, a general-purpose tar library, signing, and any sandbox were each rejected in the original.
## Packs & Extensibility

- [0004 Packs are PR-able YAML files; the database is a cache and edit layer](0004-packs-as-pr-able-yaml.md): [Accepted] `packs/*.yaml` become the source of truth for shipped packs, format frozen at v0.1, with a CI-enforced author contract (idempotent, $ARCH-aware, non-interactive, runAs-honest).
- [0013 A pack declares the values it needs; they reach every step as environment variables](0013-packs-declare-their-inputs.md): [Accepted, amended by 0014] Issue #189: an optional `inputs` list on the pack — name, label, description, `required`, `secret`, `default` — so the create form can render a field per value with no per-pack code (ADR-0004's rule again), and every bootstrap step receives them through the existing 0600 `secrets.env`, the #184 user script included. Pack-level rather than tool-level, because the delivery is pack-wide regardless and a tool-level list would describe a scoping that does not exist. Names colliding with anything Rocky Surf exports are refused at validation, and the `ROCKYSURF_`/`GIT_` namespaces were refused whole (the `GIT_` half narrowed by ADR-0014); the platform's two promised names stay a closed list, with a pack's inputs a second namespace the PACK promises. Non-secret values live on the server row (shown on its page, so a re-render months later is stable); `secret` ones live in the encrypted store under a new `pack-inputs` kind and are returned by no route. Nothing is rendered into the plan, so `PLAN_VERSION` stays 1. `secrets.env` values are now single-quoted, since a value from a form field is no longer a shape core controls. `rockysurf create --input NAME=VALUE` / `--inputs-file`, with a secret on the command line refused as `--rdp-password` already is.
- [0014 The person creating a server may set their own environment on it](0014-per-server-environment-at-create-time.md): [Accepted] Issue #197: an Environment field on the create form for every pack — `KEY=value` lines the USER types, with a `secret:` line prefix rather than a checkbox list (one control, survives a paste, and the same text `--env-file` reads). Delivered by ADR-0013's mechanism unchanged: plain values on `servers.environment`, `secret:` ones in the encrypted store under a new `server-environment` kind returned by no route, all of them through the 0600 `secrets.env`, nothing in the plan, `PLAN_VERSION` unmoved. Its own column and kind rather than sharing the pack's, because the provenance is the thing stored — the server page says which of the two a variable came from, and the same name in both is a 400 naming the key rather than a silent precedence. The name and value rules move to `env/names.ts` and are consulted by both. Answers the startup script (ADR-0011), which is stored in plain text and so had nowhere to put a token; the form's hint changes from a prohibition to a direction. `rockysurf create --env [secret:]KEY=VALUE` / `--env-file`, with a secret on the command line refused. Narrows ADR-0013's `GIT_` reservation to the four names the setup preamble actually writes, so `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME` is a name a pack or a user may now claim.
- [0018 A tool file is a sibling of a pack file, not a loosening of it](0018-a-tool-file-is-a-sibling-of-a-pack-file.md): [Accepted, "no URL arm" clause superseded by 0022] Issue #289. A second frozen format — `version: 1` plus a list of tools — reusing `toolSchema` VERBATIM, so a tool moves between a pack file and a tool file as a copy rather than a translation. Sits beside `packFileSchema` rather than making its `pack` optional, which is the option that would actually break ADR-0004's freeze (`strictObject` plus an unconditional `pack.packId` deref in the loader). Export renders one for any tool, file-backed included, stripping `sourceFile`; import writes `sourceFile: NULL` and refuses an id a file-backed tool owns, because the boot reconcile would undo the win at the next restart. `bootstrap` stays in the shared shape and `true` is refused on import, reusing `lint.ts`'s reserved-field wording. NO url-import arm, unlike packs: the `tools` table has no provenance columns, so a URL import would install root shell while being unable to say where it came from — issue #88's problem at finer granularity (SUPERSEDED by ADR-0022, which added the columns and the arm). Most of the "personal tools registry" the issue asked for already existed (`tools` table, admin CRUD, Tools page); "personal" means registered-on-this-installation, never per-user (issue #192). A tool reaches a box only through a pack (owner ruling, issue #295), and `servers.tools` now validates its ids at create time instead of silently dropping them after the instance is billing. Single-tool-pack wrapping was rejected as a format and kept as a throwaway VERIFICATION device in the `register-a-tool` skill.
- [0020 Modifying an official pack forks it, and a tool can ask to be on every box](0020-modifying-an-official-pack-forks-it.md): [Accepted] Issue #295. The owner's model is a forked repository: an official pack is never edited in place, and modifying one gives you a personal pack. `packs.derivedFromPackId` records what a fork began as — a pack id string with NO foreign key, because the boot reconcile deletes and recreates file-backed rows and an FK would either cascade a user's fork away or block the reconcile. It is provenance, not a sync relationship: nothing syncs, the fork already tracks the official tools' scripts because `packs.tools` holds ids (#204), and a parent dropped from a release leaves a dangling id that is still the only true record. A fork inherits its parent's artwork with a bright delta over the icon's top right, and ONLY a modded pack carries that delta (owner's ruling) — the parent gets a different indicator, a quieter outlined mark in the opposite corner naming the personal version, because it has a copy rather than having been modified. Opposite corners, so a fork that has itself been forked wears both with no precedence rule. Marks on the icon rather than a second badge (#192), decoration only, so the Official tab stays pristine and selectable and nothing is ever written to the official row. An exported fork carries NO inherited artwork: provenance does not export, so the delta cannot travel and unmarked official art elsewhere would be a personal pack wearing a first-party face (ADR-0006). "Add it to all packs" is `tools.alwaysInstall`, unioned in `resolvePack` AFTER its three-way branch so it reaches pack, explicit-selection and no-pack creates alike; NOT `tools.bootstrap` (reserved, wrong phase, unsmoke-testable). It is installation state, not file content, so it is absent from `toolSchema` and both file formats refuse it by construction — #298's pins pass unedited, a round trip lands on `false`, and it is the one field of a file-backed tool an operator may edit. Both upserts treat an omitted value as "leave it alone", which is load-bearing twice over: the boot reconcile would otherwise reset the flag on every shipped tool at every restart, and the admin pack PUT's whole-row literal would erase a fork's parent the first time a tool was added to it. Blast radius is disclosed twice — an always-install tool runs everywhere and ADR-0010 terminates a box whose tool install fails, so one mis-ordered tool breaks every new server — and the delete confirmation carries it because core's in-use guard scans `packs.tools` and is structurally blind to a tool no pack lists. The overlay table was rejected on four grounds, chief among them that it is invisible to `pack check` and so certifies a composition it cannot see.
- [0022 A tool can be imported from a URL, now that tools carry provenance](0022-a-tool-can-be-imported-from-a-url-now-that-tools-carry-provenance.md): [Accepted] Issue #299. Supersedes ADR-0018's "no `{ url }` arm" clause, the rest of 0018 standing. The `tools` table gains the tool equivalents of the pack registry columns — `registrySource`, `registryUrl`, `registrySha256`, `registryTrust`, `registryInstalledAt` (migration 0019) — SEPARATE columns and NOT `sourceFile`, which the boot reconcile would delete the row for (ADR-0006's trap). `POST /api/v1/admin/tools/import` then takes `{ url }`, fetched server-side through the SAME SSRF guard (`fetchPublicText`) and the same injection seam the pack import uses, never a raw fetch. A URL import records `source: 'a URL import'`, the URL, the sha256 of the exact bytes, and `trust: 'unverified'` (there is no tool registry, so no operator-written label to borrow and `official` unreachable); a paste or upload records nothing, because there is nothing true to record. Every tool in a multi-tool file shares one record — the URL and digest are of the whole file. The Tools page shows the origin ("imported from `<url>`") the way the packs page does. The refusals and strict schema are unchanged on both arms. `UpsertToolInput.registry` treats absent as "leave it alone", so the boot reconcile and the admin PUT never erase it. The shelf concept was rejected: there is no tool registry (#289 did not create one), so a tool only ever has a one-off URL. This is the change ADR-0018 deferred — the rejection there was always "not without the columns," never "not ever."
- [0006 Packs come from two places, and only the operator says which is trusted](0006-pack-registry-split-horizon.md): [Accepted] Official packs ship in the tarball; `rockysurf-shop` is community-only with no mirror. The trust label lives in the operator's config, never in a registry's index. Scanning discloses (every script verbatim, root steps, fetched URLs) rather than certifying; provenance gets its own columns because `sourceFile` would make the boot reconcile delete the pack. Format unchanged, so ADR-0004 stands. **Amended 2026-08-26 (issue #88):** a source URL ending in `.yaml` IS the pack, so a person with one file and no CI needs no `index.json`; source URLs are https-only because a pack is root shell; the source list is editable on the admin Settings page, which writes the same config file; and a URL import records the URL it came from.

## Operations & Configuration

- [0023 A backup is ciphertext plus your own config; the master key and cleartext tokens travel by your hand](0023-backup-is-ciphertext-and-your-own-config-the-key-travels-by-hand.md): [Accepted] Issue #331. Settings-page **Backup** downloads one version-stamped JSON artifact of logical rows — `secrets` rows verbatim as ciphertext (ids preserved so the GCM AAD still matches; NEVER the master key, which travels by the operator's own hand per the first-boot banner), the config file with every literal GitHub token redacted to a `${VAR}` placeholder (owner ruling: no verbatim option, no toggle; identities travel in `config.redactedTokens` so Restore lists exactly what to re-enter by name), user-owned packs/tools plus the two ADR-0020 switches on shipped ones, all server rows, users, spend baselines. Excluded: sessions, `session-signing-key` (refused inbound too), the admin password hash (anti-lockout), `events`, file-backed rows. **Restore is a merge** — id-preserving, skip-existing, refuse-with-reason (file-backed ids per ADR-0018), one DB transaction with the config write as a separate later step so nothing half-applies and a re-run is a no-op; users are reconciled by githubId (the local admin matches everywhere) and a remapped user's `github-token` is RE-SEALED under the new owner id inside `backup/restore.ts` (key absent and key wrong are one failure: drop, "reconnect GitHub") — the custody test keeps its single exemption. Records, not machines: no cloud is touched, the reconciler reports what no longer answers, ADR-0017's four pinned paths keep the TARGET's values (`server.dataDir` above all — the old path would point the next boot at an empty database), `mcp.scopes` deliberately travels. Current-month spend baseline is adjusted so restored history does not read as this month's spend (injectable clock, #284). Older-artifact-into-newer upcasts via `migrateBackup`; newer-into-older is refused with "upgrade first". The manual whole-directory tar coexists as the full-fidelity path; a passphrase-encrypted artifact, a no-secrets artifact, verbatim-config-with-warning, a toggle, replace semantics and an HTTP tar were each rejected. CLI wrappers are deferred to their own issue.
- [0017 The config file is re-read on save, and five settings say why they cannot be](0017-settings-apply-on-save.md): [Accepted, amended by 0021] Issue #264. `rockysurf.config.yaml` stops being read once at startup: the settings save re-reads it through the same `checkConfigText` the boot path uses and this process adopts it before the response is written, so a cloud switched on, a region corrected, a token rotated, a limit raised or a pack source added is in force at once. Adoption is all-or-nothing — an invalid file, or one naming a `${VAR}` this environment lacks, leaves the previous values running and says why. Four paths are PINNED to their booted values (`server.port`, `server.host`, `server.dataDir`, `auth.mode`) because the listener is bound, the database and master key are open and every live session was issued by the booted mode; `mcp.scopes` is the fifth restart case and belongs to a different process. Every field now declares `appliesAt: 'save' | 'restart'` with a reason, rendered beside the control, and the drift banner narrows to those five. The provider registry and the pack shop's client are rebuilt in place rather than re-read (`ProviderRegistry.replaceWith`), so no seam holding one is rethreaded and an in-flight call keeps the client it resolved. A file watcher, a `Proxy` over `Config` and moving settings into the database were each weighed and rejected.

## Credentials

- [0007 Two ways to hand Rocky Surf a GitHub credential, and where each one lives](0007-github-credentials-two-paths.md): [Accepted] A Connect GitHub button runs the OAuth device flow against an OAuth App the operator registers (`github.oauth.clientId`, public, no default — an official app would couple every install to a third party's registration); OAuth App over GitHub App because its user tokens do not expire. The connected token goes to the encrypted store per user, where `server-secrets.ts` already prefers it over `github.pat` and reads it live, so no restart; pasted per-repo PATs stay in the config file. rockysurf-4o3o is reversed for `github.pat` and `github.tokens.*.pat` only, via a per-field `accepts` flag — the FILE still interpolates `${VAR}` and hand-edited references still load. Disconnect forgets locally and does not revoke at GitHub.
- [0019 Saved SSH public keys are named entries in the config file, and the parser refuses the private half](0019-saved-public-keys-live-in-the-config-file.md): [Accepted] Issue #302: `ssh.keys` in `rockysurf.config.yaml` — a list of `{name, publicKey}` edited on the Settings page and offered by the New Server page's picker — stored in plain text and unmasked, because a public key is published material and encrypting one copy of it is the custody theatre ADR-0011 already named; no table, no migration, no `SECRET_KINDS` entry, and `SECURITY.md`'s inventory gains no row. `normalizeUserPublicKey` moves to a dependency-free `ssh/public-key.ts` so the schema and the create path share ONE parse, and it refuses anything containing `PRIVATE KEY` before any other check — the wrong-half paste used to be refused as a formatting error. The picker fills the existing `sshPublicKey` field and posts the KEY, never the name, so core, the row, the plan, cloud-init and ADR-0008's retirement are untouched and `PLAN_VERSION` does not move; an empty `publicKey` is legal and means "the Add button wrote this and nobody has typed in it yet". A database table, a secret kind, resolving a name in core, and shipping a real key as the Add placeholder were each weighed and rejected; the CLI and MCP are deliberately left alone, having no SSH-key argument at all. **Amended same day:** PR #303 shipped this section as two boxes of prose and no controls — `view.lists` was served by core and never read by the SPA, so every list existed only by a hand-written block, and the wiring test seeded an entry and so never asked about the empty state every install starts in. The page now draws ANY list core declares, `SETTINGS_LISTS` carries the `blank`/`labelField`/`empty` that needs (with the blank parsed through `configSchema` in `fields.test.ts`), `ssh.keys` keeps no hand-written block so the generic path ships in the product, and a card that would be a heading with no controls says so. **Amended again same day (rsui-9sc):** Add no longer writes a placeholder entry — it reveals a blank form (no default name) whose own save appends exactly what was typed; `blank` became `add` (`noun`/`example`/`required`), and an item-field `warning` (the private-key sentence) renders once at the head of the list, not under every card.
- [0016 A provisioned box holds its secrets as owner-only plaintext files](0016-secrets-on-the-box-are-plaintext-at-rest.md): [Accepted] Issue #244: runtime secrets live on the box as `0600` plaintext sourced into every shell — the disk is the trust boundary on a single-user box, matching what `gh`/`claude`/`aws` already do; process-env-only, an on-box keyring, fetch-at-login and an external manager were each weighed and rejected for adding ceremony or coupling without changing the terminal exposure.

## Operations

- [0005 The config file's home, and the order it is found in](0005-config-file-resolution.md): [Accepted] Three-tier resolution — explicit `--config` (fatal if absent), cwd file (workflow tier), `~/.rockysurf/config.yaml` (durable home, literal path, no dataDir circularity); first saves create the home file, never cwd litter; the boot notice names which loaded.
